Evidence and impact: Source plus 390px source fixture: directory988px; selected title below first viewport
Proposed remedy: Searchable grouped desktop navigation and compact mobile selected-section drawer
Priority and acceptance: P1: page content immediately reachable; preserve permission gates and keyboard focus

Evidence and impact: Mobile event/channel collision; repeated channel text and accessible names; source initial-load error branch missing.
Proposed remedy: Desktop channel headings, mobile event blocks; event-specific switch labels; titled load/error/retry.
Priority and acceptance: P1. At 390px no overlapping text; every switch identifies event/channel; failed read never spins forever.

Evidence and impact: Compact form; read-only currency looks unexplained beside copy implying management. Failed name save has no visible error branch.
Proposed remedy: Explain currency restriction and supported next step; inline recoverable save status.
Priority and acceptance: P1 feedback, P2 polish. Failure is visible and draft remains; no invented currency-edit capability.

Evidence and impact: Invite form dominates initial view; directory lacks search. Mobile directory requires substantial horizontal travel.
Proposed remedy: Directory first, focused invite action; shared identity row with name + isolated email and obvious detail action.
Priority and acceptance: P1. Search/status preserved after detail close; pending/delivery recovery clear; permissions unchanged.

Evidence and impact: Already stronger directory, search, tabs and task dialogs. Mobile tabs and wide directory need clearer access to offscreen tasks.
Proposed remedy: Reuse shared people shell; keep policy/recovery/delivery/audit distinct.
Priority and acceptance: P1 mobile, P2 consolidation. All tabs reachable by touch/keyboard; account detail has a visible entry at narrow width.

Evidence and impact: Simple list is readable; create form is always expanded. Empty table has no purpose/next-step context. Source two-step saves can partially succeed.
Proposed remedy: Focused Create → team detail/member task; useful empty state; explicit partial-success recovery; named delete confirmation.
Priority and acceptance: P1 recovery, P2 layout. Membership retry never creates a second team; Cancel never writes.

Evidence and impact: Directory/create form precede long editors for every set. Mobile is very long.
Proposed remedy: Selected-role editor, groups and change summary; deliberate save/discard/cancel on role switch.
Priority and acceptance: P1. Preserve individual flags; team means managed-team records; Admin is not falsely constrained by flags.

Evidence and impact: Compact desktop list; several repeated row actions compete with identity. Result handling and Cancel vary.
Proposed remedy: Common configuration-row editing/menu pattern with contextual action names.
Priority and acceptance: P1 silent failures, P2 layout. Failed writes visible; cancel restores name; used/system restrictions preserved.

Evidence and impact: Many controls always visible. German “Gesamtes Unternehmen”/pipeline selections truncate in desktop fixture; mobile form becomes a long stack and table is wider than content.
Proposed remedy: Focus Create/Edit: type → assignee → period → target → review; compact list summaries on mobile.
Priority and acceptance: P1. Long labels readable; original calendar/currency/number parsing retained; failed save keeps draft.

Evidence and impact: Repeated name text, color controls, actions and four entity sections create density.
Proposed remedy: Entity navigation/search, compact swatch, shared row menu/edit state.
Priority and acceptance: P2, P1 failed writes. Color/name failure is recoverable; reorder rollback explicit; no silent success.

Evidence and impact: Old Gmail surface has status but bidi/rejected-disconnect risks. New independent-mail components already improve setup, empty state, status and recovery.
Proposed remedy: Review and refine new supported mailbox flow; do not replace it with a speculative provider catalog.
Priority and acceptance: P1 acceptance, P2 polish. Distinguish saved credentials, verified connection and sync state; preserve fresh-auth and disconnection semantics.

Evidence and impact: Early entity choice is useful. Mobile row actions squeeze name/type; Add sits after lists.
Proposed remedy: Header Add, entity navigation, name-first rows and contextual actions; explicit option autosave feedback.
Priority and acceptance: P1. Full field identity discoverable at 390px; controls name the field; locked/custom/hidden distinctions retained.

Evidence and impact: Existing stepper and row diagnostics are useful. No wired Back/remap/Cancel in key forward-only steps; query failure can look empty.
Proposed remedy: Preserve stepper; reversible mapping/review before commit; raw/interpreted values together; persistent result and correction path.
Priority and acceptance: P1. Back retains mapping and invalidates old validation; no repeated commit; loading/error never means zero errors.

Evidence and impact: Actual surface is actor-scoped OAuth grants plus optional MCP help, not service integrations. Mobile URL needs readable LTR/manual-copy treatment.
Proposed remedy: Clearly name AI/MCP access; cross-link mailboxes/service connection tasks; explain revoke consequences.
Priority and acceptance: P1 clarity, P2 layout. Each revoke identifies client; clipboard failure recovers; no unsupported connectors/scopes implied.

Evidence and impact: Compact card and isolated email work. Photo/name use different save triggers, with existing explanatory copy; unchanged name Save stays enabled.
Proposed remedy: Keep layout; disable unchanged Save and show local saving/saved/error.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Unchanged disabled; failure retains draft; photo upload feedback stays distinct.

Evidence and impact: Strong grouping, status and re-verification already exist. Mobile cards stack readably; long identity is shortened.
Proposed remedy: Preserve structure and safeguards; keep security status and next action prominent; make full identity discoverable.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Both locales fit; dialog focus and native enrollment/recovery require live validation.

Evidence and impact: Readable stacked controls; preview is lower than the choices. Timezone list is limited. New rial/toman setting is independent and present.
Proposed remedy: Searchable timezone picker with localized labels and LTR IDs; adjacent contextual preview.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Language/calendar/timezone/digits/money unit remain independent and saved values survive unrelated edits.

Evidence and impact: Theme and density have different persistence models, already explained. Unchanged density Save is already disabled.
Proposed remedy: Standardize local status presentation, preserving deliberate Save-to-apply density.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Autosave and explicit save both announce success/failure without ambiguity.

Evidence and impact: Long but intelligible grouping; phone formatting and sounds mix with record behavior. Optimistic rollback already exists.
Proposed remedy: Keep behavioral preferences; consider phone under Regional and sound under Notifications with clear migration/links.
Priority and acceptance: P2. No preference loss; preserve serialization and optimistic recovery.

Evidence and impact: Clean small list, but counts/scope are hard to infer; no parent empty state. Failed member read becomes empty in source.
Proposed remedy: Explain record visibility versus membership/permissions; counts and focused detail.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Read failure is distinct from no members; add/remove retains context and recovery.

Evidence and impact: Useful stage counts and primary create already exist; repeated title/description can be calmer. Stage editing leaves settings.
Proposed remedy: Retain counts; reduce duplicate header copy; maintain return-to-settings and pipeline context.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Editor return restores selected pipeline; no stage-count feature invented.

Evidence and impact: Restrained list works; rename/archive/reorder conventions differ from related lists. Failed optimistic reorder can remain onscreen.
Proposed remedy: Shared row pattern and explicit archive consequence.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Failed reorder restores saved order; rename can cancel; archive keeps actual domain semantics.

Evidence and impact: Current paired cards are understandable at desktop; editing is a different task and busy feedback is inconsistent.
Proposed remedy: Task tabs or clear sections, focused editor and recipient-facing preview.
Priority and acceptance: P2. Slow submit cannot duplicate writes; failed save preserves draft; defaults/shared read-only behavior retained.

Evidence and impact: Useful provider readiness/cost/throttle controls already exist; mapping and cache are further down. Source clears key draft before success.
Proposed remedy: Progressive Provider → readiness → mapping → cache summary; per-provider status and intentional secret retry behavior.
Priority and acceptance: P2. No success before real check; preserve cost/quotas; failed key save is actionable without leaking secrets.
